class.why: The ABAP source writes the name lower case and the sidecar's CLSNAME upper case. Renaming half of it produces an object abapGit imports under one name and ABAP activates under another - which is the whole reason this is a script and not an instruction. The test include names the class too (the class under test, and the reference to its attributes), so it is listed here and renamed with the pair.

agentSetup.note: What `npm create abap2ui5-app@latest -- --agent-setup [dir]` adds to a project that did NOT start from this template - most abap2UI5 projects. A subset of files.shared: the agent setup (AGENTS.md, the skills with the guide, the MCP server, the permission allowlist), the two gates it tells the agent to run, and the CI job that runs them. Never files.named: an existing project has its own src/, .abapgit.xml and package. A file the project already has is skipped and named, never overwritten - except the two under `merge`, which only ever ADD what is missing. leftOut.package-lock.json: locks the TEMPLATE's package.json, which a merged one is not; `npm install` writes the right lockfile - commit it, check.yml runs `npm ci`
leftOut..gitattributes: normalises line endings for the whole repository; in an existing one that rewrites files its history holds in another form - a decision about the repository, not part of an agent setup
leftOut..github/dependabot.yml: the update policy for every npm package and action of the whole repository, which an existing project has already decided (its own file, Renovate, or none); check.yml's SHA pins work without it
leftOut..devcontainer/devcontainer.json: an editor environment, not agent or gate setup - and a project with a container has its own
leftOut..vscode/extensions.json: editor recommendations, not agent or gate setup - and a project with a .vscode/ has its own
leftOut..github/abaplint/abap_702.jsonc: the 7.02 downport config of scripts/check-702.mjs, which a project runs by hand when it targets NetWeaver 7.02 - its files glob is src/, and an existing project decides its own release targets
leftOut.scripts/check-702.mjs: the 7.02 downport check, run by hand (`node scripts/check-702.mjs`) and copying src/ - no package.json script or workflow invokes it, so an existing project that wants it copies it with the config above
leftOut..github/scripts/rename.mjs: abap2UI5's namespace rename, run by hand (`node .github/scripts/rename.mjs --name <name> --out <dir>`) when the framework is installed renamed; it reads src/ and abaplint.jsonc's framework pin and package.json config.renameOwn, which the agent-setup merge does not carry

package.json.why: each entry under these keys is added when the project lacks it and left alone when it has it, whatever its value - a project's own `check` script or abaplint version is its decision, and the create package names every one it kept. A devDependency the project lists under dependencies counts as present

.gitignore.why: the template's patterns the project does not ignore yet are appended, each with the comment above it; nothing is reordered or removed

sourceFolder.why: the template keeps its classes in src/, and four of these files say so. An existing project's .abapgit.xml says where it keeps them (STARTING_FOLDER), and a gate pointed at a src/ that is not there checks nothing - and passes. Each edit replaces `placeholder` inside the FIRST occurrence of `text`: the first `"files"` in abaplint.jsonc is global.files, the second is the framework dependency's own folder and stays

existingVariants.why: abaplint also reads abaplint.json, and many abapGit projects have one. The template's abaplint.jsonc is still added - `npm run check:abap` and the pin check read that one - and the create package says the project now has both

# AGENTS.md — abap2UI5 app template

Briefing for AI assistants (and humans) developing **this abap2UI5 app
repository**, created from
[abap2UI5/app-template](https://github.com/abap2UI5/app-template) with the
validation gates preconfigured. Two parts: this repository (yours — rewrite
it, add your own rules), then the essentials of building an app (generated).

## This repository

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/` | The app classes, one `ZCL_*` class per app (abapGit, `STARTING_FOLDER=/src/`). `zcl_app_001` is the starter app with its ABAP Unit include — copy it for a new app |
| `abaplint.jsonc` | Gate 1. Clones the abap2UI5 framework for dependency resolution, pinned to release tag `1.151.0` (key `"branch"`); `npm run check:pin` holds the places that name it to one number |
| `abap2ui5lint.jsonc` | Gate 2, the [abap2UI5-linter](https://github.com/abap2UI5/linter): every view checked statically and rendered headless |
| `.claude/skills/` | Four skills, loaded on demand: `build-an-app`, `view-chain-layout`, `abap-check`, `ui5-check` — a short `SKILL.md` each, long sections under `references/` |
| `.claude/skills/build-an-app/references/building-apps.md` | **The full app-building guide** — the one copy; its essentials are below |
| `docs/project.md` | This section in detail: every file, the gates, addons, testing, the 7.02 and rename scripts |

## Build & verify — run before every commit

```bash
npm ci                          # once - both gates, from the lockfile
npx playwright install chromium # once - the render gate needs a browser
npm run check                   # abaplint + linter, expect 0 issues
npm run check:abap2ui5:fast     # fast loop: the linter without the render gate
npm run fix                     # apply the linter's mechanical corrections
npm run test:unit               # the ABAP Unit tests, transpiled - no system
npm run check:all               # what CI runs: the pin, then both gates
npm run doctor                  # a gate failed oddly? one line per cause, with the remedy
npm run add-addon -- popups     # the app calls an addon class: register the addon
```

- A gate that names a symptom, not a cause — a syntax error inside
  `node_modules`, "browser not found", "Class z2ui5_cl_popup_... not found" —
  is what `npm run doctor` explains. It is offline and takes a second.
- Every `.clas.abap` needs its `.clas.xml` sidecar: UTF-8 **with BOM**, LF,
  `CLSNAME` equal to the file name — copy an existing one. Class names are
  `ZCL_*`/`ZCX_*`. Everything in English.
- An addon ([abap2UI5-addons](https://abap2ui5-addons.github.io/)) is a
  separate abapGit install and unknown to the lint gate until
  `npm run add-addon -- <repo>` registered it; `-- --list` shows them all.
- Without a system the gates are all there is: say which ran. Deploy with
  [abapGit](https://abapgit.org/), start with `<endpoint>?app_start=zcl_app_001`.

## What to read when

| Doing | Read |
| --- | --- |
| Writing or changing an app class | the essentials below, then the guide's section for the topic; the `build-an-app` skill is the checklist |
| Laying out a view chain | the `view-chain-layout` skill, then `npm run fix` |
| Finishing a change under `src/` | `abap-check`: its `SKILL.md`, then references 1 and 2 |
| Writing or reviewing a view | `ui5-check`: its `SKILL.md`, then reference 1 |
| A gate, the pin, an addon, a test, 7.02, a renamed framework | `docs/project.md` |

<!-- guide-essentials:begin - GENERATED from abap2UI5's docs/agents/building-apps.md by scripts/generate-agents.mjs in abap2UI5/app-template. Do not edit between this line and guide-essentials:end; put your own rules above. -->

## Building an app - the essentials

What follows is cut out of the framework's app-building guide, word for word. The whole guide is ONE file, `.claude/skills/build-an-app/references/building-apps.md`; §N below is its section N. Read the section before you rely on a line here - and the whole of §2 to §5 before a first app.

### 1. The model in one paragraph

An abap2UI5 app is **one ABAP class** implementing `z2ui5_if_app`. The
framework calls its `main( client )` method on every HTTP roundtrip, and the
app dispatches on why it was called: it has to put its view on screen
(`check_on_navigated`, true on the first start and on every return into the
app), or the user interacted with it (`check_on_event`), or it is running for
the very first time and has one-time setup to do (`check_on_init`). The first
two are the dispatcher; the third is a branch an app only carries when it has
something to seed once. All three are arms of ONE `IF`/`ELSEIF` chain (§2).
The app builds a UI5 XML view as a string, binds ABAP attributes into it,
and registers named events. Between roundtrips the framework
serializes the app object into a draft table and restores it — **every PUBLIC
attribute is persisted state and travels to the browser with the model**, so
bound data goes in `PUBLIC SECTION`, everything else in `PROTECTED SECTION`.
There is no JavaScript, no OData service and no deployment step: activate the
class, call the ICF endpoint with `?app_start=zcl_my_app`.

### 2. The canonical app template

```abap
CLASS zcl_my_app DEFINITION PUBLIC.

  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES z2ui5_if_app.
    " ONLY bound data here - PUBLIC attributes are serialized every roundtrip
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_s_item,
             product  TYPE string,
             quantity TYPE i,
           END OF ty_s_item.
    DATA t_items TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_s_item WITH EMPTY KEY.
    DATA name    TYPE string.

  PROTECTED SECTION.
    DATA client TYPE REF TO z2ui5_if_client.
    METHODS view_display.
    METHODS on_event.
    METHODS model_init.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
ENDCLASS.


CLASS zcl_my_app IMPLEMENTATION.

  METHOD z2ui5_if_app~main.

    me->client = client.
    IF client->check_on_init( ).
      model_init( ).
      view_display( ).
    ELSEIF client->check_on_navigated( ).
      view_display( ).
    ELSEIF client->check_on_event( ).
      on_event( ).
    ENDIF.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD view_display.

    DATA(view) = z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder=>factory(
        )->ele( n = `View` ns = `mvc`
            )->a( n = `xmlns`     v = `sap.m`
            )->a( n = `xmlns:mvc` v = `sap.ui.core.mvc`
            )->a( n = `displayBlock` v = `true`
            )->a( n = `height`       v = `100%`

            )->ele( `Page`
                )->a( n = `title` v = `My App`

                )->tag( `Input`
                    )->a( n = `value` v = client->_bind( name )

                )->ele( `List`
                    )->a( n = `items` v = client->_bind( t_items )

                    )->ele( `items`

                        )->tag( `StandardListItem`
                            )->a( n = `title` v = `{PRODUCT}`
                            )->a( n = `info`  v = `{QUANTITY}`

                    )->end(
                )->end(

                )->tag( `Button`
                    )->a( n = `text`  v = `Save`
                    )->a( n = `press` v = client->_event( `SAVE` ) ).

    client->view_display( view->stringify( ) ).

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD on_event.

    CASE client->get_event( ).
      WHEN `SAVE`.
        " bound data (name, t_items) already carries the user's input here,
        " and the changed model is pushed back automatically
        client->message_toast_display( |Saved, { name }| ).
    ENDCASE.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD model_init.
    t_items = VALUE #( ( product = `Notebook` quantity = 2 )
                       ( product = `Mouse`    quantity = 5 ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.

ENDCLASS.
```

- **Do:** one chain — `IF client->check_on_init( ).` (seed, then display),
  `ELSEIF client->check_on_navigated( ).` (display), `ELSEIF
  client->check_on_event( ).` (dispatch), as in the template.

### What you remember may be the old API (§3)

**Names that changed.** Most of what was written about abap2UI5 before
1.143.0 names an API that has been replaced; when one of these comes to mind,
write the right-hand side:

| Remembered | Write |
|---|---|
| `z2ui5_cl_xml_view=>factory( )->shell( )->page( )` | `z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder` as above — the legacy fluent builder (one method per control) is frozen and since 1.151.0 only exists where [abap2UI5-ext](https://github.com/abap2UI5/abap2UI5-ext) is installed |
| `_bind_edit( )`, `view_model_update( )` | `_bind( )`; delete the update call (§4) |
| a `check_initialized` flag | `client->check_on_init( )` (§2) |
| `client->get( )-event`, `get( )-t_event_arg` | `client->get_event( )`, `client->get_event_arg( )` (§5) |
| `_event_client( )` | `follow_up_action( )` (§5) |
| `nav_app_leave( client->get_app( client->get( )-s_draft-id_prev_app_stack ) )` | `client->nav_app_leave( )` (§7) |
| `z2ui5_cl_pop_to_confirm` and the other `z2ui5_cl_pop_*` | `z2ui5_cl_popup_*` of the popups addon (§6) |
| `z2ui5_cl_util=>…` | no longer in the framework and no API for apps — write the few lines yourself |

Every replaced name with old and new code:
<https://abap2ui5.github.io/docs/resources/deprecations.html>, as data
<https://abap2ui5.github.io/docs/api/deprecations.json>.

### Four rules that are cheap to break (§3, §4, §8)

- **Booleans from ABAP variables** go through `b` instead of `v`:
  `` )->a( n = `editable` b = mv_edit_mode ) `` renders `true`/`false` (a
  literal is just `` v = `true` `` — never feed `abap_true` into `v` raw, it
  serializes as `X`).
- **An element gets its attributes before its first child.** `a( )` lands on
  the element the chain is pointing at — the child just added by `ele( )` or
  `tag( )`, or the node itself while it has none. Once an element has a
  child, `a( )` can no longer reach it.
- **Never hard-code a model path as text** (`'/T_ITEMS'`): paths come from
  `_bind`, so renames cannot break bindings. For raw binding-info strings
  (typed bindings, sorters) get the bare path via
  `client->_bind_path( t_items )`, e.g.
  `` v = |\{ path: '{ client->_bind_path( t_items ) }', sorter: \{ path: 'PRODUCT' \} \}| ``.
- **State discipline**: every PUBLIC attribute is serialized into the draft
  and sent to the browser on every render. Large helper data, catalogs and
  anything not bound belongs in PROTECTED (or is re-read per request) — a
  bloated public section makes every click slower.

### An addon class the lint gate does not find (§6, §9)

- **`npm run add-addon -- <repo>`** in a project made from app-template
  (`popups`, `range-filter`, …): registers an addon, and what it depends on,
  in the dependencies of `abaplint.jsonc`, so the lint gate resolves its
  classes. Without it a call to an addon class ends in "Class ... not found" —
  which says the gate does not know the addon, not that the class is wrong.

### Where to read on

Sections of `.claude/skills/build-an-app/references/building-apps.md`:

| § | Read it for |
|---|---|
| 1 | The model in one paragraph |
| 2 | The canonical app template |
| 3 | The view builder — `z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder` - Formatting the chain (strict, and machine-checked) |
| 4 | Data binding |
| 5 | Events |
| 6 | Popups, popovers, messages |
| 7 | Multi-view, navigation, routing |
| 8 | Rules that keep apps portable |
| 9 | Validate and iterate like the framework does |
| 10 | The in-app developer tools (Ctrl+F12) - Starting them; What you find there; When they do not open |
| 11 | Calling a language model |

# This repository, in detail

The long form of the first part of [`AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md): every file of
a project made from [abap2UI5/app-template](https://github.com/abap2UI5/app-template),
the gates and how they fail, the addons, testing an app without a system, and
where the agent skills come from. `AGENTS.md` says the same in a page and is
what an agent reads first; come here for the reason behind a line of it.

## This repository

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `src/` | The app classes (abapGit project, `STARTING_FOLDER=/src/`, `FOLDER_LOGIC=PREFIX`) — one class per app, named `ZCL_*` |
| `src/zcl_app_001.clas.abap` | The starter app — rename/copy it for your first real app (keep the `.clas.xml` sidecar's `CLSNAME` in sync) |
| `src/zcl_app_001.clas.testclasses.abap` | ABAP Unit tests for the starter app: a test double for `z2ui5_if_client` drives `main( )` through the first start, a `SAVE` event and a navigated roundtrip. Runs on the system (ADT `Ctrl+Shift+F10`); the local gates check it statically — see "Testing an app" below |
| `package.json` | The two gates as devDependencies (`@abaplint/cli`, `@abap2ui5/linter` + its render runtime `@abap2ui5/linter-render`, on the same minor line — they are cut from one tag) and the `npm run check*` scripts. `package-lock.json` is committed, so CI and your machine run the same versions |
| `package-lock.json` | Committed on purpose: `npm ci` reads it, so the gate versions CI runs are the ones you ran locally |
| `abaplint.jsonc` | abaplint config; abaplint clones the abap2UI5 framework for dependency resolution, pinned to a release tag — `AGENTS.md` names it, and `npm run check:pin` holds the places that do to one number (`"branch"` — abaplint passes it to `git clone --branch`, which takes a tag; there is no `"tag"` key). The framework floor is 1.143.0: `1.142.0` has neither `z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder` nor `client->get_event( )`, both of which the starter class uses. Bump the pin when you need a newer API, and run `npm run check` |
| `abap2ui5lint.jsonc` | [abap2UI5-linter](https://github.com/abap2UI5/linter) config (paths, UI5 floor, distribution, rule severities, fail level) — CLI flags override it |
| `.github/workflows/check.yml` | CI: the framework pin, then abaplint from the lockfile, then the abap2UI5-linter through its own action (`abap2UI5/linter`, SHA-pinned) for the static gate + headless render of every view |
| `scripts/check-702.mjs`, `.github/abaplint/abap_702.jsonc` | `node scripts/check-702.mjs` — does the app downport to NetWeaver 7.02? A temporary copy of `src/` downported with `abaplint --fix` against the framework's `-702` release and linted at v702; your tree is never touched |
| `.github/scripts/rename.mjs` | abap2UI5's namespace rename, for a system where the framework is installed renamed: `node .github/scripts/rename.mjs --name /CA2UI5/ --out build/renamed` writes `src/` with every `z2ui5_` reference renamed and your own `zcl_`/`zcx_`/`zif_` objects moved into the same namespace (`package.json` `config.renameOwn`); without `--name` it checks the longest name the framework allows. Not the template's `scripts/rename.mjs` |
| `scripts/check-pin.mjs` | `npm run check:pin` — the framework release above is written in more than one place and no tool moves it; this fails when they disagree and notices (without failing) when a newer release is out |
| `scripts/add-addon.mjs`, `scripts/addons.json` | `npm run add-addon -- <repo>` — registers an addon of [abap2UI5-addons](https://abap2ui5-addons.github.io/) (`popups`, `range-filter`, …) and everything it depends on in `abaplint.jsonc`, from a vendored snapshot of the addon catalogue — see "Addons" below |
| `scripts/doctor.mjs` | `npm run doctor` — offline environment check, one line per finding with its remedy: Node version, both gates installed and on one minor line, a Chromium the render gate can launch, the framework pin, the linter Action pin against the devDependency, every `.clas.xml` sidecar (BOM, LF, `CLSNAME`, `WITH_UNIT_TESTS`), `abap2ui5lint.jsonc`, an addon class the app names that `abaplint.jsonc` does not resolve, the VS Code extension, the linter's compatibility record, whether the installed linter has `--watch`. Exit 1 only on FAIL |
| `.claude/skills/` | Four agent skills mirrored from the framework — `build-an-app`, `view-chain-layout`, `abap-check`, `ui5-check` — loaded on demand by Claude Code and any agent that reads `SKILL.md` files: a short `SKILL.md` each, the long sections as files under `references/`. Generated (each file says so in its first lines); "this repository" in their text is the framework's |
| `.claude/skills/build-an-app/references/building-apps.md` | The framework's app-building guide, whole — the one copy in this repository. `AGENTS.md` carries the essentials cut out of it |
| `AGENTS.md`, `docs/project.md` | The briefing an agent reads first — this repository in short, then the guide's essentials — and this file, the long form of its first part |
| `.claude/settings.json`, `.mcp.json` | The permission allowlist for autonomous sessions, and the abap2UI5 MCP server registered for Claude Code (`npx --yes @abap2ui5/mcp-server`). The VS Code extension registers the same server for Copilot itself |
| `.devcontainer/`, `.vscode/extensions.json` | A dev container (Node 22, both gates and Chromium installed on create, the abap2UI5, abaplint and Claude Code extensions) and the editor's extension recommendations |

## Build & verify — run before every commit

```bash
npm ci                          # once - installs both gates from the lockfile
npx playwright install chromium # once - only the render gate needs a browser

npm run doctor                  # is this machine able to run the gates? one line per check, with the remedy

npm run check                   # abaplint + linter, expect 0 issues
npm run check:abap2ui5:fast     # fast loop: linter without the render gate
npm run watch                   # the fast loop, again on every save - Ctrl+C ends it
npm run watch:render            # the same with the render gate, one warm browser across the runs
npm run test:unit               # the ABAP Unit tests in the transpiled backend - no system (see Testing an app)
npm run fix                     # apply the linter's mechanical corrections
npm run check:pin               # the framework release this repo names, in one place
npm run add-addon -- popups     # an app calls an addon class: register the addon with the lint gate
npm run check:all               # everything CI runs: the pin, then both gates
npm test                        # the same as `npm run check:all`
```

When a gate fails in a way that names a symptom rather than a cause — a
syntax error inside `node_modules` (old Node), "browser not found" (no
Chromium), a rule CI has and your run does not (Action pin and devDependency
on different minor lines), "Class z2ui5_cl_popup_... not found" (an addon the
lint gate was never told about) — `npm run doctor` says which, and what to
run. It is offline and takes a second.

`npm run watch` is `abap2ui5lint --watch --no-render`: the static check once,
then again on every save under `src/` (and on an edit to
`abap2ui5lint.jsonc`, which is read again), the report on stdout and a
separator naming the changed file on stderr; `npm run watch:render` is the
same loop with the render gate on, keeping one warm browser across the runs
instead of launching one per run. A watch never exits 1 - it is the loop for
a developer whose editor has no linter in it (Eclipse ADT, with abapGit
pulling the classes into this checkout: save, pull, read), not a gate; it
refuses `--fix`, `--screenshot` and the JSON/SARIF outputs, so `npm run fix`
stays a separate step. VS Code users have the extension's live check instead.
The flag arrived with `@abap2ui5/linter` 0.7.0; on an older linter both
scripts print its `unknown option '--watch'` and exit 2 (`npm run doctor` says
whether the installed linter has it).

`npm run check:all` is the local equivalent of the CI job — a green run of it
means CI passes. (`npm run check` is the two gates alone and skips the pin,
which is why the two scripts exist separately.)

Both gates run offline from any SAP system (abaplint clones the framework on
first use, so it needs network). Deploy to a system via
[abapGit](https://abapgit.org/) and start an app with
`<icf-endpoint>?app_start=zcl_app_001`.

While writing, the
[VS Code extension](https://github.com/abap2UI5/vscode-extension) surfaces the
same linter findings as editor diagnostics with quick fixes, and
[mcp-server](https://github.com/abap2UI5/mcp-server) gives an MCP-capable agent the
deploy → build → run-headless-and-screenshot loop.

Conventions: every `.clas.abap` needs its `.clas.xml` sidecar (UTF-8 **with
BOM**, LF endings — copy an existing one; `abaplint.jsonc` enables `xml_bom`
and `xml_consistency`, so a hand-edited sidecar fails the gate rather than the
next abapGit pull; a class with a `.clas.testclasses.abap` include also
carries `<WITH_UNIT_TESTS>X</WITH_UNIT_TESTS>` after `<UNICODE>`, which is how
abapGit serializes one); class names stay in `ZCL_*`/`ZCX_*`, which is both
`object_naming` in `abaplint.jsonc` and the rule the rename step enforces; the
whole repo is in English.

## Addons

`abaplint.jsonc` lists what abaplint clones to resolve the classes an app
calls, and out of the box that is the framework alone. A class of an addon
([abap2UI5-addons](https://abap2ui5-addons.github.io/): `z2ui5_cl_popup_to_confirm`
of popups, `z2ui5_cl_layo_manager` of layout-management, …) therefore fails
`npm run check:abap` with **"Class ... not found" — which says the gate does
not know the addon, not that the call is wrong.** `npm run doctor` names the
addon; this registers it:

```bash
npm run add-addon -- popups          # popups, and layout-management, which it needs
npm run add-addon -- --list          # every addon: what it is for, its classes, what it needs
npm run add-addon -- popups --dry    # what would change, nothing written
```

It inserts one entry per addon into `dependencies` — the addon's own
dependencies first, each once, nothing else in the file touched — and does
the same in `.github/abaplint/abap_702.jsonc`. A second run changes nothing.

**The pin.** abaplint clones a dependency with `git clone --depth 1 -b
<branch>`, and `-b` takes a branch or a tag, never a commit. So an addon that
carries a release tag equal to the framework release pinned here (today
popups, layout-management, table-maintenance and the two custom-controls
repositories, each with the tag and its `-702` twin) is pinned to that tag, and a later run moves it
along when the framework pin moved. An addon without that tag follows its
default branch (`main`, for some `standard`; `702` in the 7.02 config) and the
output and the comment in the file say **NOT pinned**: that lint can change
without a commit here. To hold such an addon at a commit, check it out
yourself at the entry's `"folder"` — abaplint reads a dependency from there
when the folder holds files and skips the clone.

**On the system an addon is a separate install.** It is a repository of its
own, pulled with abapGit after abap2UI5 and after what it depends on; the run
ends with that order. An app that calls an addon does not activate on a
system that has not pulled it — say which addons the app needs.

What the script knows is `scripts/addons.json`, a snapshot of the addon
catalogue (<https://abap2ui5-addons.github.io/addons.json>: `useWhen`,
`entryPoints`, `dependsOn`) and of each addon's branches and tags, so it works
offline and decides the same thing every time. The template refreshes it
daily; take a newer one by copying the file from the template's `main`.
`npm run test:unit` installs the framework alone — a test that reaches into
an addon class needs a system.

## Testing an app

`src/zcl_app_001.clas.testclasses.abap` shows the shape: the app talks to the
framework only through the `z2ui5_if_client` it is handed, so a local class
with `INTERFACES z2ui5_if_client PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED` — attributes deciding
what `check_on_init( )` / `check_on_navigated( )` / `check_on_event( )` /
`get_event( )` answer, tables recording what `view_display( )` and
`message_toast_display( )` were given — is the whole test bed. The three tests
are the three roundtrips every app has: the first call seeds the model and
displays a view (`<Input`, `<List`), the `SAVE` event toasts `Saved, World`,
and a navigated roundtrip re-displays without seeding again. The double
implements every method the app CALLS - the lifecycle questions, the two
things it does back, and the four the view code reaches for (`_bind`,
`_event`, `_event_nav_app_leave`, `check_app_prev_stack`): on a system a
`PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED` interface's missing methods are generated empty, in
the transpiled runtime below they are not, and a call to one is a TypeError
there. Add a method to the double when the app starts calling another one;
the runner names the missing one.

Run them on the system with ABAP Unit (ADT `Ctrl+Shift+F10`, or SE24) - or
**without a system**: `npm run test:unit` (the mcp-server's `abap2ui5-unit`)
installs the framework at the release `abaplint.jsonc` pins from the npm
package `@abap2ui5/node-runtime` (cached under `~/.abap2ui5-mcp`; a pin older
than 1.145.0 clones the release and builds its backend instead), transpiles
the classes under `src/` with their test includes into it and runs the tests
through the open-abap runtime. The `unit`
job in `check.yml` does the same on every pull request through the
`abap2UI5/mcp-server` action, with the step summary naming every test method
and the first failure. What the runtime cannot model (the abap-check skill
lists the known cases) a system still has to answer. `npm run check` stays
what it is: abaplint compiles the include against the framework's interface,
and the abap2UI5-linter skips `*.testclasses.abap`, so the render gate sees
the app class alone. The rename step renames the include with the class (it
is in `template.json`'s `substitutions.class.files`).

## Agent skills and the guide

`.claude/skills/` holds four skills an agent loads when the task matches
their description: **build-an-app** (the checklist for writing an app class),
**view-chain-layout** (the seven layout rules for a builder chain and the
linter rule that checks them), **abap-check** (ABAP that a green CI does not
catch: abapGit round trip, activation, extended check, runtime) and
**ui5-check** (the same for the view: names that do not exist on the oldest
supported UI5 release, layout that needs a newer one).

Each is a short `SKILL.md` — the two catalogues with a table that says which
file to read when — and its long sections as files under `references/`, so an
agent that is told to run `abap-check` reads the two sections every app needs
and not the framework's downport pipeline. The framework's guide to building
an app is one of those references,
`.claude/skills/build-an-app/references/building-apps.md`, and it is the only
copy here: `AGENTS.md` carries the passages the guide itself marks as
essential, cut out word for word between its two `guide-essentials` marker
lines, and a table of the guide's sections.

All of it is mirrored from
[abap2UI5/abap2UI5](https://github.com/abap2UI5/abap2UI5) by the template's
generators — the skills from its `skills/` folder, the guide and the
essentials from its `docs/agents/building-apps.md` — with a declared handful
of sentences reworded (`npm run fmt:chains` is `npm run fix` here; the guide
file lists its own in its header). Where a skill says "this repository" or
names a `.github/scripts/` gate, it means the framework's. Fix them upstream;
a regeneration overwrites the copies (the template regenerates its mirrors
daily and opens a pull request when abap2UI5 changed them; a project made
from it takes newer text by copying the files from the template's `main`).
Your own rules for agents go into `AGENTS.md`, outside the two marker lines.

Starting a project without this repository's own scaffolding: `npm create
abap2ui5-app@latest my-app -- --class zcl_my_app` writes the same files from
the template's `main` branch (see the template's README for the four ways).
Adding this setup to a project that did not start from the template: `npm
create abap2ui5-app@latest -- --agent-setup` in its directory writes the agent
files and the gates (`template.json`'s `agentSetup` says which), skips every
file the project already has, and only adds to `package.json` and
`.gitignore`.

files..github/workflows/check.yml:
# The two gates every abap2UI5 app repo gets for free - both run without an
# SAP system:
#
#   abaplint       - ABAP syntax and style, with the abap2UI5 framework cloned
#                    as a dependency so z2ui5_* names resolve
#   abap2ui5lint   - the abap2UI5-linter: the app class and the view it builds,
#                    checked together (controls, properties, UI5 version floor,
#                    bindings, builder-tree defects) plus a headless
#                    XMLView.create render of every view
#
# The two halves are run differently, and the reason is worth knowing before
# you copy this file:
#
#   abaplint runs from THIS repository's devDependencies (`npm ci` below), so
#   the version CI uses is the version `npm run check` uses on your machine -
#   package-lock.json decides both.
#
#   the abap2UI5-linter runs as its own GitHub Action, `abap2UI5/linter`. The
#   action brings its own install plus the ~118 MB UI5 runtime and the Chromium
#   the render gate needs, which is what makes three steps of a hand-rolled
#   workflow into one. Every input left unset falls back to this repository's
#   `abap2ui5lint.jsonc`, so paths, UI5 floor, distribution, rule severities and
#   the fail level are still decided by the config in this repo - not by the
#   workflow, and not by the action.
#
#   That does mean the linter version CI runs comes from the action pin, not
#   from package-lock.json. The pin below is the action's release on the
#   same minor line as the `@abap2ui5/linter` devDependency - keep the two
#   moving together, or a local `npm run check` and this job can eventually
#   disagree about a rule. They HAD parted: the pin sat on v0.2.1 while the
#   devDependency asked for ^0.2.2, one patch apart in the direction this
#   comment warns about. The template's own check-template gate now checks the
#   pairing rather than asking anyone to remember it.
#   (`abap2UI5/linter@v0` is the shorter, always-current form; this repo pins,
#   see below.)
#
# The actions below are pinned to a COMMIT rather than to `@v7`/`@v0`, and the
# repository you make from this template inherits that. A major tag is a
# pointer its owner can move, so a job runs whatever it points at that day;
# a commit cannot change under you. The tag stays in the comment so the
# version is still readable, and `.github/dependabot.yml` (also inherited)
# moves the pins - a pinned action does not become a stale one. (Pinning
# `abap2UI5/linter` pins what that action DOES; the `actions/setup-node` it
# uses internally is still the action's own choice.)
name: check

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: check-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'npm'

      # No dependencies, so it runs before the install: the framework release
      # this repository pins and the releases its prose names have to be one
      # number. This step, and every script it names, is part of what a project
      # made from this template receives - see scripts/check-template.mjs, which
      # fails when a handed-out file invokes one that stays behind.
      #
      # It also reports a newer framework release when it can reach GitHub - as
      # a notice, never as a failure. See scripts/check-pin.mjs.
      - name: Framework pin
        run: npm run check:pin

      # id, because the job-summary step below runs `npx abap2ui5lint` from
      # the devDependency this installs. Gated on this outcome rather than on
      # `always()`: without the install npx falls through to the registry,
      # where the package does not exist, and the run's last words are
      # `404 'abap2ui5lint@*' is not in this registry` - which names neither
      # the real failure nor this step.
      - id: install
        run: npm ci

      - name: abaplint (expect 0 issues)
        run: npx abaplint abaplint.jsonc

      # Settings come from abap2ui5lint.jsonc, which asks for the render gate
      # ("render": true) - so a runtime that failed to install fails this step
      # instead of being skipped with a warning under a green check. Findings
      # are annotated onto the pull request diff automatically.
      #
      # Useful inputs this deliberately does NOT set: `paths`, `min-ui5`,
      # `fail-on` (all read from abap2ui5lint.jsonc), `render: false` (a much
      # faster property-only job, no UI5 runtime, no browser), `screenshots:
      # build/screenshots` (photographs every checked view, for an
      # upload-artifact step to publish - it runs even when the check failed).
      - name: abap2UI5-linter (property gate + headless render)
        uses: abap2UI5/linter@2e084670c4442055cd18b74fccde3c2288c1d0e0 # v0.11.1

      # The same report as markdown on the run's own page - property gate only,
      # since the step above already decided whether the views load. This one
      # runs from the repo's own devDependency: the action reports into the log
      # and onto the diff, and has no input that writes a job summary.
      - name: Job summary
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && steps.install.outcome == 'success' }}
        run: npx abap2ui5lint --no-render --advisory --no-progress --format markdown >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The ABAP Unit tests of the app classes, without a SAP system: the
  # mcp-server's runner installs the framework at the release abaplint.jsonc
  # pins (the same pin the job above lints against) from the npm package
  # @abap2ui5/node-runtime - no framework clone; a pin older than 1.145.0, the
  # first release with that package, takes the old clone-and-backend path -
  # transpiles every class under src/ with its *.clas.testclasses.abap into it
  # and runs the tests through the open-abap runtime. The install is cached per
  # pin, so a run after the first pays only the transpile. The step summary
  # names every test method and the first failure.
  #
  # A separate job on purpose: it needs neither the gates' npm install nor a
  # browser, and a failing test should read as a failing TEST, not as a red
  # lint. What it cannot see is what the runtime cannot model (a real system
  # answers that - and the abap-check skill lists the known cases); a
  # PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED test double has to implement every method the code
  # under test calls, because the runtime generates no empty stubs. Locally:
  # `npm run test:unit`.
  #
  # Pinned to a commit like the other actions, and moved by dependabot the same
  # way; `abap2UI5/mcp-server@v1` is the always-current form (the floating
  # major tag mcp-server's release moves to every 1.x; `@v0` stays at 0.3.0).
  unit:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: abap2UI5 unit tests (transpiled backend, no system)
        uses: abap2UI5/mcp-server@bb9851a1e11b86fd662cc1a65f34c10b7e62331c # v1.0.0
        with:
          paths: src
files..github/dependabot.yml:
# Monthly dependency updates, opened as pull requests so the check workflow
# decides whether they are safe.
#
# This file is part of the template on purpose. The two gates are pinned
# through package-lock.json - `npm ci` reads the lock, so the version in it is
# the version your CI and your `npm run check` actually run - and a pin that
# nobody moves is a pin that silently ages out of the rules it was meant to
# apply. This is the smallest thing that keeps it current: one grouped pull
# request a week, with your own checks deciding.
#
# Weekly rather than monthly on purpose: a month of gate releases arrives as one
# lump nobody reviews line by line, and the two gates here move often enough
# that the lump is the normal case rather than the exception.
#
# Change the day, widen the interval, or delete the file - it is yours now.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: npm
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      time: "06:30"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      gates:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["minor", "patch"]
      gates-major:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["major"]

  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
      time: "06:30"
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      actions:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["minor", "patch"]
      actions-major:
        patterns: ["*"]
        update-types: ["major"]

# Building an abap2UI5 app

**Read `references/building-apps.md` next to this file (the framework's
guide, shipped with this skill) — it is the complete
self-contained guide** (template, lifecycle, builder verbs, binding rules,
events, popups, navigation, portability rules, validation tooling). This
skill is the trigger and the checklist; the guide is the content.

**Before writing one from scratch, ask whether it exists.** `abap2UI5/samples`
holds 150 working apps, each linted, rendered and downported to three
releases — a value help, a tree, navigation between two apps, a dynamic table
typed at runtime. Reading one beats reproducing it, and beats any snippet: the
sample is gated, a snippet is a copy somebody has to keep in step.

- With the [MCP server](https://github.com/abap2UI5/mcp-server): the `examples`
  tool queries that catalogue (`examples { query: "value help f4" }`) and
  hands back the class to read. Its neighbour `capabilities` answers the other
  question — whether a UI5 *control* can be expressed at all — out of
  samples-controls' 622 ports.
- Without it: [SAMPLES.md](https://github.com/abap2UI5/samples/blob/main/SAMPLES.md)
  is the same catalogue as a page.

**The same question for a dialog, a table layout the user saves, a selection
screen or a lock: the addons.** They are finished classes in repositories of
their own under [abap2UI5-addons](https://github.com/abap2UI5-addons) —
`z2ui5_cl_popup_to_confirm` and its siblings in popups, for one. The catalogue
for agents is <https://abap2ui5-addons.github.io/llms.txt> (as data:
<https://abap2ui5-addons.github.io/addons.json>). An addon is a separate
abapGit install; in a project made from app-template,
`npm run add-addon -- <repo>` registers it so abaplint resolves its classes
(guide §6 and §9).

The rules that go wrong most often. Each is one line here and a section of
the guide — read the section before you rely on the line.

- **What you remember may be the old API.** `z2ui5_cl_xml_view`,
  `_bind_edit( )`, `view_model_update( )`, a `check_initialized` flag,
  `z2ui5_cl_pop_*` and `z2ui5_cl_util` are all replaced or gone — the table
  "Names that changed" in guide §3 says what to write instead.
- **One class implements `z2ui5_if_app`; `main( client )` runs once per
  roundtrip and is ONE `IF`/`ELSEIF` chain**, so exactly one arm runs:
  `IF client->check_on_init( ).` seeds and displays, `ELSEIF
  client->check_on_navigated( ).` displays, `ELSEIF client->check_on_event( ).`
  dispatches. The navigated arm is not optional — it is the roundtrip a
  called app or a value help hands control back on. An app with nothing to
  seed drops the init arm. Never separate `IF` blocks, never one nested in
  another (guide §2; the linter's `missing-view-display-on-navigated`,
  `redundant-init-display`, `separate-lifecycle-ifs`).
- **Ask the lifecycle with the call itself**: `IF client->check_on_init( ).`,
  never `IS INITIAL` / `IS NOT INITIAL`. A negative branch, and every other
  `abap_bool`, is compared: `= abap_false`.
- **PUBLIC attributes are serialized, browser-visible state.** Bound data
  only; everything else PROTECTED.
- **Build views with `z2ui5_cl_ui5_view_builder`** (`ele`/`tag`/`a`/`end`/
  `stringify`). The legacy `z2ui5_cl_xml_view` is frozen — never in new code.
- **`a( )` has three value parameters**: `v` for constants, bindings and
  events; `b` for a boolean from an ABAP variable (`abap_true` in `v`
  serializes as `X`); `t` for text that carries data, which the builder
  escapes so a `{` in it is not read as a binding (guide §3).
- **The chain's layout is strict and machine-checked — the `view-chain-layout`
  skill is the single source of the rules**, the `factory( )` shape that goes
  with each chain shape included (the linter's `chain-house-layout` rule:
  `npm run check:abap2ui5` reports,
  `npm run fix` applies). Write the chain, run the formatter, read the
  diff.
- **Bind with `client->_bind( var )`**, display-only included; `_bind_edit`
  is removed. Row-template fields bind as `` `{UPPERCASE}` ``. Never write a
  model path as a text literal. A value the view shows is bound, not baked
  into the view — changed bound data is pushed automatically, and
  `view_model_update( )` is removed (guide §4).
- **Events**: `client->_event( `NAME` )`, dispatched with
  `CASE client->get_event( ).`. Client-resolved arguments are `$`-prefixed;
  an argument that carries data goes on a wire with
  `s_ctrl-check_arg_literal = abap_true`; a per-keystroke wire (`liveChange`,
  `liveSearch`, `sliderChange`) sets `s_ctrl-check_queue_last` (guide §5).
- **Popups**: `popup_display( val = … )`, but `popover_display( xml = …
  by_id = … )`. A button that only closes is
  `follow_up_action( val = cs_event-popup_close )`, not a backend event
  (guide §6).
- **Thin frontend**: business logic is computed in ABAP and bound, never put
  into a formatter. UI5 1.71 is the floor — check "available since"
  (the `ui5-check` skill).
- **The app checks its own authorizations** at the top of `main`.
- Validate with the abap2UI5-linter
  (`npm run check:abap2ui5`, or `npm run check:abap2ui5:fast` without the
  render gate); iterate without a SAP
  system via the mcp-server (`deploy_app` → `build_backend` → `run_app`,
  then `interact_app` to drive the event branch and `run_unit_tests` for
  the class's own test double — guide §9 has the tooling and the double).
- Before you finish, go through sections 1 and 2 of the `abap-check` skill —
  the abapGit round trip and activation. They catch what a green lint does
  not; its other sections are for the cases their headings name.
- The API contract is `src/02/z2ui5_if_client.intf.abap` in
  [abap2UI5/abap2UI5](https://github.com/abap2UI5/abap2UI5/blob/main/src/02/z2ui5_if_client.intf.abap) — when unsure about
